description: Oil & Gas Watch, run by the Environmental Integrity Project, spotlights the environmental impact of the oil, gas and petrochemical buildout in the United States through a database and map of facilities and projects. In October 2022 it added more than 100 new and proposed pipeline routes, an ongoing effort with FracTracker Alliance and Healthy Gulf. Routes were digitised with GIS from paper or PDF maps in permitting documents such as FERC environmental impact statements, or taken from state agencies such as the Texas Railroad Commission and the Louisiana Department of Natural Resources; examples include the Mountain Valley Pipeline, pipelines serving the Plaquemines LNG export terminal and the 580-mile Matterhorn Express. A map layer records where and when each route was obtained. The database is available online free of charge; no data licence is stated on the pages read, and questions go to an EIP email address. Coverage is the United States. Caveats: it focuses on new and proposed projects and expansions, not all existing pipelines; only new segments of expansion projects are shown; routes may change as projects progress; and accuracy and resolution vary by source. The main site is a JavaScript application that could not be read as text. Simulation uses are locating planned oil, gas and petrochemical infrastructure for future exposure and siting studies. Related records: data-npms-national-pipeline-mapping-system maps existing regulated pipelines.
